section_summary.extract_value: This discussion reports a single study conducted in Hong Kong examining the factorial validity of a Chinese version of the BAS, finding a two-dimensional factor structure and a truncated 7-item General Body Appreciation factor with good internal consistency and construct validity. The study used a student sample (limiting generalisability), found men had slightly higher General Body Appreciation than women, and recommends the 7-item measure for Cantonese-speaking samples while urging further cross-cultural validation and examination of BAS-2.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'The present study sought to examine the factorial validity of a Chinese version of the BAS among a sample in Hong Kong.'; 'The present study arrived at a two-dimensional factor structure of the BAS in a sample of adults in Hong Kong.'; 'A strength of the present work is the large sample size... Conversely, however, the reliance on a student sample limits the generalisability of our findings.'; 'we found that men in Hong Kong had significantly higher General Body Appreciation than women.'

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single study examining the factorial validity of a Chinese version of the Body Appreciation Scale in a Hong Kong student sample, reporting a two-factor solution with a truncated 7-item General Body Appreciation factor. The authors note gender invariance, small higher scores in men, limitations due to the student (college) sample and translation/dialect issues, and recommend further cross-cultural validation (including of the BAS-2).
